porbos.title: On the Road to ‘Umrah, Quraysh’s Obstruction • The Pledge Under the Tree • The Terms of the Treaty, the Demand to Change the Name

blocks.0: On the Road to ‘Umrah, Quraysh’s Obstruction
blocks.1: The sixth year of the Hijrah. The Prophet {{1}} set out from Madinah with about fourteen hundred Companions, in ihram, with sacrificial animals along. One purpose only, the tawaf of the Ka‘bah, ‘umrah. A few days’ journey from Madinah. After stopping at a place by the road, news came that Quraysh had sent ahead a party of horsemen under Khalid ibn al-Walid. Khalid was not yet a Muslim. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.3: Khalid ibn al-Walid is at al-Ghamim with the cavalry vanguard of Quraysh. Take the right-hand road.{{1}}
blocks.4: Khalid did not even notice, until, seeing the dust of the Muslim army, he rushed to inform Quraysh. The army turned and descended into a mountain pass by which one can go down to the lower side of Makkah. Not wanting war, he had been avoiding the possibility of fighting. But to avoid it, if the road plan had to be changed, he changed it. The intention was peace, yet the eyes were open. The two go together.{{1}}
blocks.5: We often choose one of two directions. Either we walk with eyes closed in simple trust, or in suspicion we raise the sword at everyone. The Prophet {{1}} did neither. To avoid a quarrel, sometimes the very path must be turned; not meeting face to face is also an act of wisdom. As soon as they reached the pass leading down toward Makkah, the Prophet’s {{2}} she-camel Qaswa’ sat down and did not rise again. The people said, Qaswa’ has become stubborn. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.7: Qaswa’ has not become stubborn, that is not her nature; she was held back by the One who held back the elephant. By the One in whose hand is my soul, whatever proposal they ask of me in which they honour the sanctities of Allah, I will give it to them.{{1}}
blocks.8: Though every reason for fighting was at hand, he decided beforehand: where the sanctity of what Allah has made sacred is protected, he would make concessions. For the one who holds power, making concessions is not weakness. News came that Quraysh were ready with weapons and would not let them enter the Ka‘bah. Envoys came and went. The Prophet {{1}} pitched his tent at the far end of Hudaybiyah, and repeatedly gave the same message, we have not come to fight, we have come to perform ‘umrah. At Hudaybiyah there was only one well. Fourteen hundred people and their camels, drawing water, until the well went completely dry, not a single drop remained. The news went to the Prophet {{2}}. Al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA) said,
blocks.10: He came and sat at the edge of the well. He asked for a vessel of water and made wudu’, rinsed his mouth, made du‘a, then poured the water into the well. We left the well alone for a little while. Then that well gave us and our mounts as much water as we needed.{{1}}
blocks.11: The enemy ahead, the road to the Ka‘bah closed, the well dry too. At the most helpless moment Allah showed that for the one with whom He is, no road is closed. And this same Companion used to say later, you count the conquest of Makkah as the conquest; we count as the conquest the Bay‘at al-Ridwan (the Pledge of Allah’s Pleasure) of the day of Hudaybiyah. The day that everyone then thought a defeat, for those who were there, that was the real victory. When we have nothing in hand we do the most reckoning, where will it come from, who will give. The Prophet {{1}} sat by the dry well. He used what he had: one vessel of water, wudu’, du‘a. Taking the tiny thing in one’s hand and raising the hands toward Allah.
blocks.12: The Comings and Goings of the Envoys
blocks.13: First came Budayl ibn Warqa’ of Khuza‘ah; he reported that Quraysh had gathered all their strength and would not let them enter the Ka‘bah. The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.15: We have not come to fight anyone, we have come to perform ‘umrah. War has consumed Quraysh, wounded them badly. If they wish I will make a truce with them for a fixed term, they will leave me and the rest of the people alone. And if they refuse, then by the One in whose hand is my soul, I will fight them for this call of mine until my neck is severed.{{1}}
blocks.16: First the offer of peace, thinking of the enemy’s losses; but on the question of the call there is no compromise. Gentle words and an unshakeable decision, the two together. Then came ‘Urwah ibn Mas‘ud; what he said on seeing the Companions’ love has been told in dars one. Then came a chief of Banu Kinanah. The Prophet {{1}} said, this is a man of a tribe that honours sacrificial animals; take the animals before him. The line of animals garlanded around the neck passed before him, and the Companions welcomed him reciting the talbiyah. In astonishment he declared Allah’s glory and burst out, it is not right to turn these people away from the Ka‘bah. Going back he told Quraysh, I have seen the garlanded, marked animals; I do not think it right to hold these people back. No argument, no speech; only opening the purpose before the eyes. Speaking to each person in the language that person understands. Then came Mikraz ibn Hafs. Seeing him the Prophet {{2}} said, this is Mikraz, a wicked man. He came and began to speak.{{3}}
blocks.18: In the middle of the talks the Prophet {{1}} had sent ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA) as an envoy to Makkah. He was delayed in returning, and a rumour spread that Quraysh had killed him.{{2}}
blocks.19: The Prophet {{1}} sat under a tree and took the pledge of the Companions. Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) was asked later, upon what did you pledge that day? He said, upon death. Jabir (RA) used to say, we were fourteen hundred; we pledged that we would not flee.{{2}}
blocks.20: The job of holding the branch aside was Ma‘qil ibn Yasar’s (RA); so that it would not touch the Prophet’s {{1}} head. ‘Umar (RA) was holding the Prophet’s {{2}} hand that day, Jabir (RA) said.{{3}}
blocks.21: His name is not written large in history. Yet the small task of holding a branch aside entered the picture of the pledge. We wait for a big task and leave the small one at hand lying. Yet the weight of a task is judged not by how small it is, but by for whom it is. Everyone pledged. Except one. Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari hid with his head tucked under his camel’s belly.
blocks.23: We all pledged, except Jadd ibn Qays al-Ansari; he hid under the belly of his camel.{{1}}
blocks.24: One among fourteen hundred. Everyone stretched out their hands, he kept his head tucked down. If one in a crowd lags behind, the crowd loses nothing. But the picture of hiding at the call of duty in the end became his identity. And ‘Uthman (RA) was not there, in Makkah. Everyone pledged. Then the Prophet {{1}} placed one of his hands on the other and said, this is ‘Uthman’s hand. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) said later,
blocks.26: The Prophet {{1}}, with his right hand, said, this is ‘Uthman’s hand. Then, placing the left hand over it, he said, this is on behalf of ‘Uthman.{{2}}
blocks.27: The one who is not present, his share too he took for himself. Stretching out the hand on behalf of the absent is the Prophet’s {{1}} model. In our gatherings, who says a good word on behalf of one who is not there? In one’s mouth the word of death, in another’s the word of not fleeing; the aim is one, not to turn back before the enemy. The Qur’an has told of this pledge like this,
blocks.29: Surely Allah was pleased with the believers when they pledged allegiance to you under the tree. He knew what was in their hearts. So He sent down tranquility upon them and rewarded them with a nearby victory.{{1}}
blocks.30: The pledge taken for death, in its place Allah gave pleasure and the good news of a nearby victory; that victory was Khaybar, the very next year. ‘Uthman (RA) had not been killed; the rumour was false. But the worth of the pledge did not diminish. Allah saw the readiness of the heart, not the outcome. The Prophet {{1}} said later,
blocks.32: Allah willing, not one of those who pledged under the tree will enter the Fire.{{1}}
blocks.33: Often our preparation is tested with a danger that in the end does not come at all. Because the danger did not come, the preparation is not wasted; what gets written with Allah is that day’s intention alone. There is another thing about this tree. The next year the Companions returned by that road. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) said,
blocks.35: The next year we went back, but not even two men of us could agree on the tree under which we had pledged. It was a mercy from Allah.{{1}}
blocks.36: Which tree it was, no one could say for sure. Ibn ‘Umar (RA) called it Allah’s mercy. The place of the tree under which such a great event happened, forgotten; so that people remember not a tree but the pledge.
blocks.37: The Terms of the Treaty, the Demand to Change the Name
blocks.38: ‘Uthman (RA) returned safely. Now Quraysh sent Suhayl ibn ‘Amr, to write the treaty. Seeing him coming the Prophet {{1}} said, your affair has now become easy. Even in the name there is a kind of good omen; Suhayl, ease. The writing began. The Prophet {{2}} said, write, Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. Suhayl said, what is al-Rahman, I do not know; write, Bismika Allahumma, as you used to write before. The Muslims said, we will write only Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. The Prophet {{3}} said, write Bismika Allahumma. Then he said, write, this is the treaty that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, has made. Suhayl objected, if we knew you were the Messenger of Allah, we would not have kept you from the Ka‘bah, nor fought you; write, Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah. The Prophet {{4}} said,
blocks.40: By Allah, I am certainly the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me. Write, Muhammad ibn ‘Abdillah.{{1}}
blocks.41: ‘Ali (RA) was writing then. He did not agree to erase the word ‘Rasul Allah’; the Prophet {{1}} told him to point out the place, then erased it with his own hand.{{2}}
blocks.42: The terms were finalised. This year they must go back without performing ‘umrah; next year they may come and stay three days. If anyone of Quraysh became Muslim and went to Madinah he must be returned; if anyone came from Madinah to Makkah Quraysh would not return him. And for ten years there would be no war between the two sides.{{1}}
blocks.43: Hearing the condition of returning, the Companions were stunned. They asked, O Messenger of Allah, shall we write this too? The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.45: Yes. Whoever of us goes to them, Allah Himself has removed him. And whoever of them comes to us, Allah will make for him a way of release.{{1}}
blocks.46: In the very condition that seemed the greatest loss, he placed two things. The one who leaves Islam and goes to them, we have no need of him. And the one who comes to us oppressed, Allah will open his way. How the condition later came undone has come in the story of Abu Basir. Another fruit of the treaty was in the enemy’s house too. The Qur’an has said it like this,
blocks.48: It is He who held their hands back from you and your hands back from them in the valley of Makkah, after He had given you the upper hand over them. Allah was seeing all that you were doing.{{1}}
blocks.49: A group of people of Makkah had come down with weapons, to attack the Prophet {{1}} and the Companions if they got the chance. They were caught. The Muslims had full power in their hands. Yet Allah so set the minds that no hand was raised. They were released. Releasing after having them in hand. The Qur’an calls this Allah’s own doing. When we get the chance we settle accounts; at home, at the office, in dealings. Releasing an opponent who has come into one’s hands is not an easy task.{{2}}
blocks.50: Agreeing to change the name, erasing a word; in none of this was there any lack of faith. What is written on paper does not change prophethood. Where conceding keeps the real thing intact, insisting on words is rather the path of losing something big. Whose obstinacy it was that day, and whose patience; the Qur’an has told it like this,
blocks.52: When those who disbelieved set in their hearts zealotry, the zealotry of the Jahiliyyah, then Allah sent down His tranquility upon His Messenger and the Muslims, and kept them firmly on the word of taqwa; and they were indeed the more deserving of it and worthy of it. Allah is All-Knowing of everything.{{1}}
blocks.53: Objection to the word ‘Rahman’, objection to the word ‘Rasul Allah’; on one side Jahili pride. On the other, tranquility, which Allah Himself sent down. Keeping a cool head in a moment that feels humiliating is not weakness; it is the sakinah given by Allah. From outside the treaty looked one-sided. Inside it was the opposite. For the first time Quraysh sat at the treaty table with the Muslims, as equals. Until then they had counted the Muslims as the dust of the road; this time they had to write a treaty naming them. No war for ten years means for ten years no way to block the call. And the number that was fourteen hundred on the day of the treaty became ten thousand on the day of the conquest of Makkah.{{1}}
blocks.54: A treaty is to be measured not by looking at the paper of terms, but by looking at the result. Often the concession that feels like a loss comes back later as the greatest win.

footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731 (the order of the envoys: Budayl, ‘Urwah, the man of Banu Kinanah, Mikraz, then Suhayl; the Kinani man’s ‘it is not right to turn these people away from the Ka‘bah’ and about Mikraz ‘rajulun fajir’). Ahmad 15259 (Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: chain hasan). Calling Jadd a ‘hypocrite’ is the view of the Sirah and of some scholars; in the text of Sahih Muslim only ‘was hiding’. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 560 (he was a hypocrite, in these words).

Note 16: by ‘the nearby victory’ the conquest of Khaybar is meant.

Ahmad 13827 (Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: sahih on the condition of Muslim). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 567 (the same sentence).
footnotes.18: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:24, p. 375 (read from the printed page).
footnotes.19: Sahih Muslim 1808 (from Anas ibn Malik (RA)): ‘Eighty of the people of Makkah came down from the mountain of Tan‘im with weapons, intending to attack the Prophet {{1}} and his Companions unawares; he seized them in peace (peacefully), spared them (let them go); then Allah revealed the verse.’ Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, 48:24, p. 375; note 22 (p. 375): while ‘Uthman (RA) was in Makkah fifty of Quraysh had come to carry out a secret attack, the Muslims caught them; Allah made the Muslims’ mood favour not killing the prisoners. (In number, ‘eighty’ in Muslim, ‘fifty’ in the Tawdih; the numbers of the two narrations have not been reconciled, so no number is given in the talk.)
footnotes.20: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:26, p. 377 (Taqi ‘Uthmani; checked against the rendered PDF). Note 27: the objection to writing Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim and Rasul Allah when writing the treaty was due to Jahili pride and self-conceit; the Companions were very angry, Allah gave them extra forbearance, that is the ‘sakinah’. Note 28: ‘the word of taqwa’ means obedience to Allah and the Messenger in all circumstances, however unpleasant.
footnotes.21: Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 565–568 (‘The Essence of the Treaty’; Quraysh’s recognition, the ten-year truce, the path of spreading Islam, the result: in just two years the number from three thousand to ten thousand). The figure is al-Rahiq’s calculation: ‘at some moments no more than three thousand, within just two years of the conquest of Makkah ten thousand’. Verse Tawbah 9:13 (‘they were the ones who first began the quarrel with you’), which al-Rahiq quotes.

quiz.q: When Qaswa’ sat down, the Prophet ﷺ said, she was held back by the One who held back whom?
quiz.e: ‘Habis al-Fil’, the One who held back the elephant.

quiz.q: To avoid Khalid ibn al-Walid’s horsemen, which road did the Prophet ﷺ tell them to take?
quiz.e: ‘Take the right-hand road’ (Sahih al-Bukhari 2731).

quiz.q: What does the incident of avoiding Khalid’s horsemen at al-Ghamim by taking the right-hand road teach?
o: With trust in Allah there is no need to choose a path
Fighting the enemy is always inevitable
With the intention of peace, caution goes too
quiz.e: The intention was peace, yet the eyes were open.

quiz.q: Changing the path on a hint of danger fits with which instruction?
o: Allah will bring out His way
quiz.e: Caution and the intention of peace together.

quiz.q: Speaking to each person in the language that person understands; which incident is the lesson of?
o: The chief of Kinanah and the animals
quiz.e: The purpose was opened before his eyes.

quiz.q: Who was sent as an envoy to Makkah, about whom the rumour of killing spread?
quiz.e: ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan (RA).

quiz.q: In the words of Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA), upon what was the pledge made?
quiz.e: Salamah (RA) said, upon death.

quiz.q: How did the Prophet ﷺ take the pledge on behalf of ‘Uthman (RA)?
o: By sending a letter to Makkah
By calling his own right hand ‘Uthman’s hand
quiz.e: Raising his right hand he said, this is ‘Uthman’s hand.

quiz.q: Who held the branch of the tree away from above the Prophet’s ﷺ head on the day of the pledge?
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1858.

quiz.q: Who was hiding under the camel’s belly at the time of the pledge?
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1856 (Jabir (RA)).

quiz.q: Saying ‘this is ‘Uthman’s hand’, what did the Prophet ﷺ do?
o: Announced a separate pledge in ‘Uthman’s name
Placing the other hand above, took the pledge on ‘Uthman’s behalf
Left ‘Uthman off the list of the pledge
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 4066, 3698 (Ibn ‘Umar (RA)).

quiz.q: The next year, about the tree, what did Ibn ‘Umar (RA) say?
o: The tree had been cut down, so it could not be recognised
Everyone recognised the tree easily, so the pledge was taken again
A new pledge was taken again under the tree
Not even two men could agree; this was Allah’s mercy
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2958.

quiz.q: Even after it became known that ‘Uthman (RA) had not been killed, why did the worth of the pledge not diminish?
o: Allah gives value to the readiness of the heart
Another pledge was taken anew later
The rumour was in fact true
quiz.e: The verse says: Allah knew what was in their hearts.

quiz.q: In placing his hand on ‘Uthman’s (RA) behalf, what distinction of his is revealed?
o: He had failed in the duty of envoy
He had been left out of the pledge
Included in the pledge even while absent
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ called his own hand ‘Uthman’s hand.

quiz.q: How do Salamah’s (RA) ‘upon death’ and Ma‘qil’s and Jabir’s ‘upon not fleeing’ narrations fit together?
o: Two sides of the same pledge
One only of the Muhajirun, the other of the Ansar
quiz.e: Scholars’ reconciliation: the pledge not to flee is itself the preparation for death.

quiz.q: In the incident of ‘this is ‘Uthman’s hand’, what model of the Prophet ﷺ is caught?
o: Remembering the share of the absent too
Taking all decisions with his own hand
quiz.e: The share of the one not present, the Prophet ﷺ himself took.

quiz.q: A colleague at work deliberately avoided a meeting and hid; which picture of the pledge fits with this?
quiz.e: Everyone stretched out hands, he kept his head tucked down (Muslim 1856).

quiz.q: In place of ‘Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim’, what did Suhayl ask to be written?
quiz.e: He said, as you used to write before, Bismika Allahumma.

quiz.q: According to the treaty, how many days could they stay in Makkah the next year?
quiz.e: The condition was to stay three days the next year.

quiz.q: When did the Prophet ﷺ say ‘whoever of us goes to them, Allah Himself has removed him’?
o: While writing the condition of returning
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1784.

quiz.q: Why was there no harm to prophethood in erasing ‘Rasul Allah’ from the treaty?
o: The word was written again later
Suhayl acknowledged it with his mouth
The treaty never came into effect
Prophethood does not change by words on paper
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ himself said, I am the Messenger of Allah, even if you deny me.

quiz.q: What did the Tawdih al-Qur’an mean by ‘holding the hands back’ in Fath 48:24?
o: Not killing prisoners even with power
quiz.e: Note 22 (p. 375): Allah made the Muslims’ mood favour not killing the prisoners.

quiz.q: As a ‘result’ of the treaty, which matter does al-Rahiq al-Makhtum mention?
o: Madinah’s boundary growing up to Makkah
Followers from three to ten thousand
quiz.e: After the treaty in just two years the number grew to nearly ten thousand.

quiz.q: In a hard decision at the office, loss seems first and gain later; which matter does this fit?
quiz.e: A treaty is to be measured by the result, not by the terms.

quiz.q: The lesson of not taking revenge even after getting power is in the background of which verse?
quiz.e: Allah held back the hands, even after granting power.

porbos.title: Abu Jandal’s Chains • ‘Umar’s Question • The Days After the Treaty • Three Commanders from Quraysh’s House

blocks.1: The treaty had not yet been fully written. Suddenly, stumbling in chains on his feet, Abu Jandal ibn Suhayl arrived, Suhayl’s own son. He had escaped from the lower side of Makkah, and came and fell down among the Muslims. Suhayl said, Muhammad, this is the first condition about which I am making a pact with you; return him. The Prophet {{1}} said, we have not yet finished writing. Suhayl said, then by Allah, I will not make peace with you on anything. The Prophet {{2}} said, release him for my sake. Suhayl said, I will not. Abu Jandal (RA) cried out,
blocks.3: O Muslims, I have come as a Muslim, and still I am to be returned to the polytheists? Do you not see what I have suffered?{{1}}
blocks.4: The narrator says, he had been tortured severely in the way of Allah. Yet he had to go back.{{1}}
blocks.5: The Prophet {{1}} said to him, Abu Jandal, be patient, hope for reward; Allah will bring out a way of release for you and for the weak ones with you. We have made peace with them, given our word in Allah’s name, we will not betray them.{{2}}
blocks.6: Before his own eyes a Muslim brother had to be sent back with his chains. Had he broken his word that day no one would have blamed the Prophet {{1}}; on the contrary everyone would have said, he took the side of the oppressed. Yet the word was kept. Because keeping a given word never depends on convenience.
blocks.7: In our lives too there are words which, if broken, no one would know, no one would even blame us, on the contrary we would gain. That is exactly where one can tell whether I keep the word out of fear of people or for Allah.
blocks.9: Seeing the terms, seeing Abu Jandal sent back, the Companions’ hearts grew heavy. ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) went to the Prophet {{1}}.
blocks.11: Are you not truly the Prophet of Allah? He said, certainly. ‘Umar said, are we not on the truth and the enemy on falsehood? He said, certainly. ‘Umar said, then why should we accept this humiliation in our religion? He said, I am the Messenger of Allah, I do not disobey Him, and He is my helper. ‘Umar said, did you not tell us that we would go to the Ka‘bah and perform tawaf? He said, I did; but did I say, this very year? ‘Umar said, no. He said, you will go there, and you will perform tawaf.{{1}}
blocks.12: ‘Umar (RA) then went to Abu Bakr (RA) and asked the same questions. Abu Bakr (RA) gave exactly the same answers, then said, hold fast to his stirrup; by Allah, he is on the truth. ‘Umar (RA) used to say later, for those words of that day I performed many deeds.{{1}}
blocks.13: Even in the heart of the one whose faith is firmest, questions arise. Questions arising is no fault; the fault is not accepting after getting the answer. ‘Umar (RA) asked, accepted the answer, and made atonement for his haste with deeds.
blocks.14: And Abu Bakr’s (RA) answer was an exact echo of the Prophet’s {{1}} answer. When trust is this deep, on hearing the question one can tell what the answer will be.
blocks.15: The ‘Fath’ (Victory) That Descended on That Very Journey
blocks.16: On the way back, ‘Umar (RA) himself told of one night. He was travelling beside the Prophet {{1}} on a journey. He asked a question three times; the Prophet {{2}} did not answer even once. ‘Umar (RA) scolded himself, may ‘Umar’s mother lose you, you pestered the Messenger of Allah {{3}} three times, and did not get an answer even once! He spurred his camel and went ahead of the Muslims. He feared lest a Qur’anic revelation come down about him. Hardly a little time had passed when someone began to call him. ‘Umar (RA) thought, surely a revelation has come down about him. He went to the Prophet {{4}} and gave salam. The Prophet {{5}} said,
blocks.18: Tonight a surah has been revealed to me. It is dearer to me than everything on which the sun rises.{{1}}
blocks.19: Then he recited, Inna fatahna laka fathan mubina. The Qur’an says like this,
blocks.21: (O Messenger!) Know for certain that We have granted you a clear victory, so that Allah may forgive your past and future faults, complete His favour upon you and guide you on a straight path; and (so that Allah) may help you with a help that prevails over all.{{1}}
blocks.22: The journey that many thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Victory’.{{1}}
blocks.23: We pass judgment on seeing the headline; loss, defeat, failure. Yet the journey that many had thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Victory’. What is now seeming a loss, what its name is in Allah’s reckoning, we do not know. The Qur’an did not hide the Companions’ state of mind either. With faces full of grief and sorrow they said, we have come to know what Allah will do about you; what about us? Then the next verses came down: for believing men and women, gardens beneath which rivers flow. The grief did not have to be held in. The Qur’an recorded the words of the Companions’ sorrowful faces, and sent glad tidings along with it. We hide the pain of the heart, or pour it out to the wrong people. Those who were able to tell their pain to Allah, their answer came. And the Qur’an also reminded of the dream. Before the journey the Prophet {{1}} had seen in a dream that he was entering al-Masjid al-Haram with the Companions. Did that dream turn out false? The Qur’an informed,
blocks.25: Indeed Allah showed His Messenger the true dream, which was entirely real. You will surely enter al-Masjid al-Haram in safety, with (some of) you having your heads shaved and (some) with hair cut short, without fear. Allah knows what you do not know. So before the fulfilment of that dream He ordained a nearby victory.{{1}}
blocks.26: The time was not stated in the dream. ‘This very year’ was our own reckoning. Allah’s word comes true in Allah’s time. The next year that dream was fulfilled; the nearby victory was Khaybar.
blocks.28: When the writing of the treaty was done the Prophet {{1}} said, rise, sacrifice, shave your heads. No one rose. He said it three times, still no one. Everyone’s heart was broken. The Prophet {{2}} went to Umm Salamah (RA) and told her what had happened. She said, go out without saying anything to anyone, sacrifice your own animal, call a barber and have your head shaved. The Prophet {{3}} did exactly that. The moment they saw it everyone rose and sacrificed, and began to shave one another’s heads, as if in grief they would kill one another.{{4}}
blocks.29: Where saying a thing again and again does not work, doing it oneself and showing it works. And on one wife’s one counsel that day a great crisis passed; there is nothing to belittle in the words of the people of one’s household. The Companions sacrificed one camel for seven persons; a cow also for seven. Among his own animals the Prophet {{1}} placed one camel of Abu Jahl, which had a silver ring in its nose. The aim was to anger the polytheists. The chief’s camel is today among the sacrificial animals of Allah’s House.{{2}}
blocks.30: Then the Prophet {{1}} made du‘a for those who had shaved their heads. The Companions said, and those who cut their hair short? He again made du‘a for those who shaved. The Companions said it again. The fourth time he said, for those who cut short too.
blocks.32: May Allah have mercy on those who shave their heads.{{1}}
blocks.33: At first only the names of those who shaved. The Companions spoke up, and those who cut their hair short? He did not discard this word of the Companions, in the end he included them too in the du‘a. He respected the words of the Companions’ mouths. When we are grown we discard the words of the young; of a child, of a subordinate, of a new colleague. We set aside, saying we will listen later. The Prophet {{1}} listened up to the fourth time, until the Companions’ word found a place inside the du‘a. On that very journey a Companion had a head infested with lice. Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah (RA) was suffering while in ihram. The Prophet {{2}} saw and said, are the lice on your head troubling you? He said, yes.
blocks.35: Shave your head. Then fast three days, or feed six poor people, or sacrifice one sheep.{{1}}
blocks.36: Shaving the head is forbidden in ihram. But because of hardship that too was relaxed, with an easy path of fidyah. That verse of al-Baqarah came down in this very situation of Hudaybiyah; what the rule is for people halted by obstruction is also stated there. An easy path had been kept within the rule itself for hardship. Sometimes we place on ourselves such severity as is not a command. Where an easy path is open there is nothing in adding hardship of our own invention. In the terms of the treaty was the matter of returning men. Now women came. Some believing women migrated from Makkah and came to Madinah; their relatives came and asked for them back, citing the condition. The Prophet {{1}} did not return them. Because the language of the condition was for men. And now the Qur’an itself gave the instruction,
blocks.38: O you who believe! When believing women come to you as emigrants, test them. Allah knows best their faith. Then if you know them to be believers, do not send them back to the disbelievers. They are not lawful for the disbelievers, nor are the disbelievers lawful for them.{{1}}
blocks.39: The conditions of that test the Qur’an has told like this,
blocks.41: O Prophet! When believing women come to you to pledge allegiance that they will not associate anything with Allah, will not steal, will not commit adultery, will not kill their children, will not bring any slander that they fabricate between their hands and feet, and will not disobey you in anything good, then accept their pledge and ask Allah’s forgiveness for them. Surely Allah is Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.42: No shirk, no theft, no adultery, no killing of children, no false slander, no disobedience in good. The test of a woman’s faith is the measure of her character. The test of women was the pledge by word of mouth. ‘A’ishah (RA) said, the Prophet’s {{1}} hand never touched any woman’s hand; he only said in words, I have taken your pledge. Another change came inside the home. ‘Umar (RA) that day divorced his two polytheist wives. Later Mu‘awiyah ibn Abi Sufyan married one, and Safwan ibn Umayyah the other. As soon as the Qur’anic command came down, even the closest bond was let go.{{2}}
blocks.43: A person whose name is not on the paper of the pact can be endangered by the force of letters. The Prophet {{1}} kept the letter of the condition, but did not return people who were not caught by the letter. The person who is not on the paper of our dealings, is he absent from our conscience too?
blocks.45: After returning to Madinah, Abu Basir (RA) of Quraysh became Muslim and escaped and came. Behind him Quraysh sent two men; reminded of the pact. The Prophet {{1}} handed him over to them. Reaching Dhu al-Hulayfah they sat down to eat dates. Abu Basir (RA) said to one, by Allah, your sword seems excellent. The man drew it from the scabbard and said, yes, I have tested it many times. Abu Basir said, let me see it a little. As soon as it was in his hand he struck him; the man lay dead right there. The other ran away, reached Madinah and ran into the mosque. The Prophet {{2}} said on seeing him, this one has seen something frightening. The man said, by Allah, my companion has been killed, and he will kill me too. Behind him came Abu Basir (RA) and said, O Prophet of Allah, Allah has fulfilled your obligation; you did indeed return me, then Allah saved me from their hands. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.47: Woe to his mother! A kindler of war; if only he had someone with him!{{1}}
blocks.48: Hearing the words, Abu Basir (RA) understood that he would be sent back again. He went out, straight to the seashore. The Prophet {{1}} could not keep him in Madinah, because of the treaty; yet he did not punish him either. In one sentence he made it understood: there is no place here, but you are not alone. Keeping the letter of the treaty, and keeping the way of the oppressed open from within it; both together. Abu Jandal (RA) too rushed from Makkah and joined him. After that whoever of Quraysh became Muslim went and joined them there. Slowly a band came to stand; the caravans of Quraysh going toward Sham they would block. In the end Quraysh themselves, appealing in the name of Allah and kinship, sent word to the Prophet {{2}}; call them in, from now on whoever comes to you is safe.{{3}}
blocks.49: The condition that had first seemed most one-sided, in the end Quraysh themselves asked to have it taken back. The pact was not broken, yet a way came out; that word given to Abu Jandal, Allah will bring out a way, came true.
blocks.51: The Treaty of Hudaybiyah bent the backbone of Quraysh. And in the very days after that treaty three of Makkah’s sharpest men found their own way: ‘Amr ibn al-‘As, Khalid ibn al-Walid and ‘Uthman ibn Talhah. ‘Amr’s story begins earlier, after the Trench. He was then Quraysh’s diplomat. He went to the Najashi of Habashah, with a scheme. There was the Prophet’s {{1}} envoy ‘Amr ibn Umayyah. He told his companions, I will ask for him and cut off his neck. The Najashi, hearing it, grew angry. He said,
blocks.53: Do you ask me to hand over to you the envoy of a man to whom comes the great Namus, the one who used to come to Musa, so that you may kill him? ‘Amr, listen to me, follow him. By Allah, he is surely on the truth.{{1}}
blocks.54: ‘Amr (RA) himself said, hearing this, everything changed inside me. I said, will you take my pledge on his behalf, for Islam? The Najashi said, yes. He stretched out his hand, I pledged for Islam. From his companions he hid his Islam. Then he set out toward the Prophet {{1}}, to accept Islam. On the way he met Khalid ibn al-Walid. A little before the conquest of Makkah. Khalid was coming from the direction of Makkah, the Khalid who on the day of Uhud was leader of Quraysh’s horsemen. ‘Amr said, Abu Sulayman, where? Khalid said,
blocks.56: By Allah, the road has become straight. The man is certainly a prophet. I am going, by Allah, to accept Islam. How much longer?{{1}}
blocks.57: ‘Amr said, I too have come to accept Islam. The two reached Madinah together. ‘Uthman ibn Talhah was with them too.{{1}}
blocks.58: Khalid went forward first to the Prophet {{1}}. He accepted Islam, pledged. Then ‘Amr. He said, O Messenger of Allah, I will pledge on the condition that my earlier sins are forgiven; I do not speak of what comes after. The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.60: ‘Amr, pledge. Islam wipes out all that was before it, and hijrah wipes out all that was before it.{{1}}
blocks.62: Those who had once raised swords against the Prophet {{1}} came and stood before him. The past became a burden to no one. Islam gave a chance to begin anew. These three did not say the same thing. ‘Amr found the way in the Najashi’s anger. Khalid found it in his own conscience. But on the lips of both there was one phrase: how much longer? We too grasp the truth. But about accepting it we let the days lie, saying we will do it later. In the uproar of battle truth does not enter the ear; in the days of peace the heart learns to listen. The fruit of the treaty is not only on the paper of terms, but in the hearts of these people.

quiz.q: Whose son was Abu Jandal (RA)?
quiz.e: He was the son of Suhayl, the very one making the treaty.

quiz.q: I have given someone my word, now keeping it is my loss, and no one will know if I break it; what should be done according to this dars?
o: If no one knows, breaking is fine
If there is loss, the word is void
Get someone else to keep the word
Accept the loss and keep the word
quiz.e: The incident of Abu Jandal is the answer.

quiz.q: Which surah did the Prophet ﷺ speak of to ‘Umar (RA) at night?
quiz.e: ‘Tonight a surah has been revealed to me’ (Bukhari 4177).

quiz.q: What becomes clear from ‘Umar’s (RA) questions?
o: Questions arising is no fault, not accepting the answer is the fault
Asking questions is a sign of weak faith
Questions do not arise in the minds of great Companions
The right answer to a question is always found immediately
quiz.e: He asked, accepted the answer, then made atonement in deeds.

quiz.q: In the Prophet’s ﷺ answer ‘did I say, this very year?’, what misunderstanding was corrected?
o: Denying the promise of tawaf altogether
Binding the promise’s time to one’s own assumption
quiz.e: The promise was true; ‘Umar (RA) himself had assumed the time.

quiz.q: Why did ‘Umar (RA) become afraid on asking at night and getting no answer?
o: Because the Prophet ﷺ was angry
Fear of losing the way at night
Fear of a revelation coming down
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 4177.

quiz.q: What does the Tawdih al-Qur’an note say about the dream in Fath 48:27?
o: The dream was fulfilled that very year
The time was not fixed; fulfilled the next year

quiz.q: When a question arises in the mind about the decision of a great person, what is the etiquette according to this dars?
o: Ask directly and accept the answer
Keep the question suppressed and stay quietly displeased
quiz.e: ‘Umar (RA) asked, then accepted.

quiz.q: If the fulfilment of some promise of Allah seems to be coming late, which thing needs to be remembered?
o: The promise itself was perhaps misunderstood
Not binding the time to one’s own assumption
It is better to give up waiting
quiz.e: ‘Did I say, this very year?’

quiz.q: The glad tidings of the journey that many had thought a defeat fit with which event?
quiz.e: The journey many thought a defeat, the very name of its surah is ‘Fath’.

quiz.q: When the Companions hesitated at the command to sacrifice, whose advice did the Prophet ﷺ take?
quiz.e: Umm Salamah (RA) advised, to sacrifice himself and show it.

quiz.q: Where did Abu Basir (RA) finally take refuge?
quiz.e: He took refuge on the seashore.

quiz.q: According to Mumtahanah 60:10, what is the instruction about emigrant women?
o: They must be returned according to the condition, no exemption
If tested and found believers they may not be sent back
If the husband comes to take her, the woman will have the option to go back of her own will
They are to be returned only if the mahr is not returned, otherwise not
quiz.e: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, pp. 528–529.

quiz.q: What did ‘Umar (RA) do that day?
o: Returned both women’s mahr to the polytheists
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 2731–2732.

quiz.q: What was sacrificed for seven persons at Hudaybiyah?
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 1318 (Jabir (RA)).

quiz.q: Among the conditions of the women’s pledge in Mumtahanah 60:12, which one is there?
o: Going back to the disbelieving husband
quiz.e: Shirk, theft, adultery, killing children, slander, disobedience in good; Bukhari 4891.

quiz.q: Why did Umm Salamah’s (RA) advice work?
o: The Companions obeyed Umm Salamah more
This time the Prophet ﷺ spoke in harsh words
Doing it oneself and showing draws more than words
The mood lightened because Quraysh had left
quiz.e: As soon as the Prophet ﷺ himself sacrificed, everyone rose.

quiz.q: In the incident of Abu Basir (RA), what was the outcome of the one-sided condition?
o: The Muslims broke the treaty and kept him
The condition was made even stricter
No more questions were raised about the condition
Quraysh themselves asked for the condition to be taken back
quiz.e: Because of obstruction to their caravans, Quraysh themselves asked.

quiz.q: What can be understood from the du‘a for those who cut their hair short, at the Companions’ request?
o: Cutting short is better than shaving
The du‘a is only the right of those who shave
The du‘a was a strict rule
quiz.e: The fourth time he said, for those who cut short too (Bukhari 1727).

quiz.q: From the incident of Ka‘b ibn ‘Ujrah, what is the ruling on shaving the head in ihram because of hardship?
o: Never to be shaved under any condition
May not shave except after the sacrifice
quiz.e: Fidyah of fasting, charity or sacrifice (Bukhari 1814; Baqarah 2:196).

quiz.q: When one has to accept an apparently one-sided settlement, what hope does this dars give?
o: A one-sided settlement is always ultimately harmful
Settlements should be broken as soon as the chance comes
With patience a way comes out from within
quiz.e: The condition that seemed one-sided, Quraysh themselves asked to have it taken back.

quiz.q: Which is an example of putting Allah’s command before close relationships?
quiz.e: After the Qur’anic command came down, ‘Umar (RA) did exactly that.

quiz.q: If someone is turned away by mistake, finding a way to set it right oneself later fits with which incident?
o: The incident of the ring’s three-line design
quiz.e: From within the condition itself the oppressed one’s way opened.

quiz.q: A little before the conquest of Makkah, on the way to accept Islam, what question did Khalid ibn al-Walid ask ‘Amr ibn al-‘As?
o: Did I say, this very year?
Are we not on the truth?
quiz.e: ‘Fa-hatta mata?’; Ahmad 17777.

quiz.q: Against putting off accepting a truth one has understood, saying ‘I will do it later’, which statement comes to mind?
quiz.e: An example of recognising the truth and not delaying.

porbos.title: Letters to the Heads of State • The Killing of Abu Rafi‘ • Final Word • Practical Resolve

blocks.0: Letters to the Heads of State
blocks.1: The Treaty of Hudaybiyah brought a safe time. The Prophet {{1}} used that time; he wrote letters to Kisra, Qaysar, the Najashi and every powerful ruler around, calling them to Allah.
blocks.3: As soon as letters came up, the Companions said, the rulers of Rome do not read any letter without a seal. The Prophet {{1}} then had a silver ring made. Anas (RA) said, I can still seem to see its white gleam in the Prophet’s {{2}} hand.
blocks.5: I can still seem to see its white gleam in the hand of the Prophet {{1}}; its design was ‘Muhammad Rasul Allah’.{{2}}
blocks.6: The design was in three lines. Above ‘Muhammad’, in the middle ‘Rasul’, below ‘Allah’. And the Prophet {{1}} had said that no one else should make this design. Reaching the rulers in the very manner in which they read letters. Taking into account the etiquette of the one being called. We often take speaking in our own way as honesty. If we first think in what language, in what manner the one who will listen understands, the word reaches.{{2}}
blocks.8: To al-Muqawqis, the ruler of Egypt, Hatib ibn Abi Balta‘ah (RA) took the letter. In the letter the same call: accept Islam, you will be safe; Allah will give you double reward. Hatib (RA) said to al-Muqawqis, before you in this Egypt there was a man who thought himself the great lord. Allah seized him in both places, this world and the Hereafter. Take a lesson from another’s end; let not others take lesson from your end. al-Muqawqis said, we too have a religion. We will not leave it unless we find something better. Hatib (RA) said, I call you to Islam. As on Musa’s lips was the good news of ‘Isa’s coming, on ‘Isa’s lips was the good news of this Prophet. We are not asking you to turn away from the Christian religion; we call you to a more complete path. al-Muqawqis thought for a long time. Then he said, I have thought about this Prophet. I have seen that he does not call to anything disliked, nor forbid anything liked. He is not an impostor, nor a soothsayer. He gives true news of hidden matters, he foretells. I will think more. He kept the letter carefully in an ivory box, sealed it and gave it into a maidservant’s hand. Then he called a scribe who knew how to write Arabic and had a reply written. In the reply was, I knew that a prophet was yet to come, but I thought he would come from Syria. I have honoured your envoy. I am sending for you two maidservants of great honour among the Copts, some cloth and a mule for riding. al-Muqawqis did not advance even one step beyond this. He did not accept Islam.{{1}}
blocks.9: We often take courteous behaviour as consent. When someone speaks with a smile, sends a gift, honours the envoy, we think, he agrees. al-Muqawqis did everything: he thought, he honoured, he sent gifts. But he did not move from his place. Courtesy and decision are not the same thing. Even within a good reply there can be a ‘no’.
blocks.10: Abu Sufyan in the Court of Heraclius
blocks.11: Heraclius, the emperor of Rome, was then in Sham. When the letter arrived he enquired whether anyone from this man’s land was nearby. At that time Abu Sufyan was in Sham with a trade caravan of Quraysh, not yet a Muslim. He was called to the court.{{1}}
blocks.12: Heraclius said, which of you is the closest relative of this man? Abu Sufyan said, I. He seated him in front, his companions behind him; he told them, if he lies, you will point it out. Abu Sufyan used to say later, if not for the shame of being known as a liar, that day I would have lied about him. Then question after question. How is his lineage? High lineage. Has anyone among you made such a claim before? No. Was any of his forefathers a king? No. Who follows him, the influential or the weak? The weak. Are his followers increasing or decreasing? Increasing. Does anyone turn back resentful toward this religion after accepting it? No. Before the claim, did you ever accuse him of lying? No. Does he break promises? No; now we are in a term of a treaty with him, we do not know what he will do in it. Abu Sufyan used to say, apart from this one sentence I found no chance to insert anything anywhere else. Have you fought him? Yes. What was the result? Sometimes he wins, sometimes we. What does he tell you to do? He says, worship Allah alone, associate no one with Him, give up what your fathers used to say; pray, speak the truth, be chaste, maintain kinship.{{1}}
blocks.13: The man who was then one of the Prophet’s {{1}} greatest enemies, who even had the wish to lie, from his own mouth that day, in the enemy’s court, came the testimony of prophethood. Such is the force of truth; even the one who wants to suppress it, it makes open his mouth.
blocks.14: And ‘Does he break promises? No.’ This answer came right in the middle of the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, the treaty in which Abu Jandal had to be returned. The witness to keeping the word that day was the enemy’s own mouth.
blocks.16: Having heard everything Heraclius explained one by one. Prophets come from just such lineage; if it were a royal line it could be said, he wants a lost kingdom; the man who does not lie to people will not lie about Allah; the followers of prophets are the weak; faith grows exactly like this, once it sits in the heart it does not leave; prophets do not betray. Then he said, if what you say is true, he will become owner even of this place under my two feet. I knew he would come; but I did not think he would come from among you.{{1}}
blocks.17: The letter was read out. A short letter, every word measured and placed.
blocks.19: Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim. From Muhammad, servant of Allah and His Messenger, to Heraclius, the ruler of Rome. Peace upon whoever follows guidance. Now then, I call you with the call of Islam. Accept Islam, you will be safe; Allah will give you double reward. And if you turn away, the sin of your subjects too will fall upon you.{{1}}
blocks.20: At the end of the letter was a verse of Surah Al ‘Imran; the call to that common word of the People of the Book, worship of none but Allah alone. No threat, no entreaty; a clear proposal and its consequence. As soon as the reading of the letter ended an uproar rose in the court, Abu Sufyan and his men were thrown out. Coming out, Abu Sufyan said to his companions, the affair of Ibn Abi Kabshah has become very big; even the king of Banu al-Asfar fears him. He used to say, from that day I was certain he would be victorious; in the end Allah put Islam into my heart.{{1}}
blocks.21: Heraclius recognised the truth, but drew back out of fear of losing kingship. Abu Sufyan accepted nothing that day, but the seed had been sown. Recognising the truth is one thing, the courage to accept it another.
blocks.23: A letter went to Kisra, the emperor of Persia, too. ‘Abdullah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi (RA) took the letter. He had been told to give it into the hand of the ruler of Bahrain; he delivered it to Kisra. Kisra read it and tore the letter into pieces. Hearing the news the Prophet {{1}} made du‘a that they too be torn completely to shreds.{{2}}
blocks.24: There is a report of what happened next. A Persian man came to the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} said to him, my Lord has killed your lord, that is Kisra, tonight. ‘My Lord’ means Allah. ‘Your lord’ means Kisra, whom the man took as lord. The Prophet’s {{3}} Lord is one. He was also informed that Kisra had made his daughter his successor. He said,
blocks.26: A people that makes a woman its ruler never succeeds.{{1}}
blocks.27: The treasures too the Prophet {{1}} had spoken of, in another hadith of Sahih al-Bukhari: when Kisra is destroyed there is no Kisra after him, when Qaysar is destroyed there is no Qaysar after him; and their treasures will certainly be spent in the way of Allah.{{2}}
blocks.28: The one who tore the letter, his empire was in fact torn to shreds before two decades had passed. To insult a call that comes with respect is really to tear one’s own fate. In anger we too tear up letters received, throw away advice received. But if what was written in the letter was true, tearing does not change the truth.{{1}}
blocks.30: To al-Mundhir ibn Sawa, the ruler of Bahrain, al-‘Ala’ ibn al-Hadrami (RA) took the letter. al-Mundhir read the letter out to all the people of Bahrain. Many were glad and accepted Islam, many disliked it and moved away. al-Mundhir wrote, in my area there are fire-worshippers and Jews too; let me know your view about them. The Prophet {{1}} wrote the reply, I have accepted your recommendation about your people. Leave those who have accepted Islam on their Islam. I have forgiven the offenders, accept that from them. As long as you remain on the path of peace and good, you will not be removed from your post. And whoever of the Jews or fire-worshippers wants to remain in his religion must pay the jizyah. To Hawdhah ibn ‘Ali, the ruler of Yamamah, Salit ibn ‘Amr (RA) took the letter. The word of the letter was, my religion will soon reach as far as the hoof of the camel or the horse can reach. Accept Islam, you will be safe; your kingdom will remain yours. Hawdhah gave Salit the honour of a royal guest. After reading the letter, going neither right nor left, he wrote a middling reply, the path you call to is very beautiful. The Arabs fear me; give me some responsibility, I will follow you. The Prophet {{2}}, hearing the reply, said, even if he asks for a piece of land, I will not give it to him. He will perish himself, and what is in his hand will perish too.{{3}}
blocks.31: al-Mundhir and Hawdhah both received the same call. One read it out to everyone; the other wanted to bargain. Faith is not a thing to be shared out. We often put even the truth up for price. Let this much right be mine, let that much be conceded, then I will accept. But the truth that is accepted only on conditions is no longer the accepting of truth, it is dressing one’s own interest in the mask of truth.
blocks.33: To al-Harith ibn Abi Shimr, the Ghassanid ruler of Damascus, Shuja‘ ibn Wahb al-Asadi (RA) took the letter. In the letter was, believe in Allah alone, who has no partner; your kingdom will remain yours. al-Harith threw the letter far away. He said arrogantly, who will snatch my kingdom from me? I will set out against him right now. He asked the emperor of Rome for permission to fight the Prophet {{1}}. Qaysar stopped him. al-Harith sent Shuja‘ ibn Wahb (RA) off with clothes and expenses.{{2}}
blocks.34: Fear of losing kingship and the promise of protecting kingship; both were in the same letter. The language of the letter was soft. But to an arrogant mind even soft words feel like fire. We measure others’ words with our own fear. The man who is saying, it will be good for you, in fear and suspicion we hear, he wants to remove me.
blocks.36: The Prophet {{1}} sent a small group of the Ansar to the Jew Abu Rafi‘. The leader of the group was ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik (RA). Abu Rafi‘ used to hurt the Prophet {{2}} and help his enemies against him. He lived in a fortress of the Hijaz. The sun had set. The people were returning home with livestock. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik said to his companions, you sit here. I will go and try to get in by some stratagem with the gatekeeper. Going near the gate of the fortress he sat covering his head with his cloth, as if relieving himself. The gatekeeper called, servant of Allah, if you want to enter, enter, I will close the gate. He went in and hid. Everyone entered, the gate was closed. The gatekeeper hung the bunch of keys on a peg. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik went and took the key, and opened the gate. Abu Rafi‘’s night gathering sat on the upper floor. The gathering broke up. He went upstairs. He would open one door, bolt it from inside; then another. He thought, even if people notice they will not be able to catch me before I reach Abu Rafi‘. A dark room. Abu Rafi‘ in the middle of the family. In which corner, impossible to tell. He called, Abu Rafi‘! A reply came, who? He struck toward the voice. It did not work. Abu Rafi‘ cried out. He came out. After a while, changing his voice, he entered again and asked, what is that noise, Abu Rafi‘? He said, woe to your mother! Someone in the room struck me with a sword. ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik struck again; still it was not finished. Then he set the tip of the sword in the belly and pressed, it went to the back. He understood the job was done. He began going down opening the doors one after another. Reaching near the stairs he thought he had reached the ground. He put his foot down. A moonlit night. He fell. The shin of his leg broke. He took off his turban and bound the leg. Then he walked and sat near the gate. He said, I will not go out tonight until I am sure I have killed him. The rooster crowed. On the fortress wall a herald stood and announced, I announce the death of Abu Rafi‘, the merchant of the Hijaz. Only then did he return to his companions. He said, hurry, Allah has finished Abu Rafi‘. Reaching the Prophet {{3}} he told it all. The Prophet {{4}} said,
blocks.38: Stretch out your leg. I stretched out my leg. He wiped it; as if nothing had ever happened to me.{{1}}
blocks.40: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik could have fled. His leg broken, the night deep. But he sat until the sure news came in the herald’s voice. We often spread news on mere hearsay; even before the rooster crows. He sat on his broken leg only to make one matter firm. And coming back with the broken leg he went first to the Prophet {{1}}. News of the work, news of the pain, both to be taken to the one to whom they should be taken. That leg was healed by his touch.
blocks.42: Some pictures stay fixed in the mind from this journey of Hudaybiyah. A she-camel sitting down at Hudaybiyah, and right after it the declaration, I will accept any proposal in which the sanctities of Allah are honoured. Fourteen hundred hands under the tree, the vow not to flee up to death. Erasing ‘Rasul Allah’ from his own name, because it takes nothing away from prophethood. Abu Jandal in chains, and a prophet forced to return him, who did not break his word. ‘Umar’s question and Abu Bakr’s exactly identical answer. A crisis passed by one counsel of Umm Salamah. And in the court of Heraclius the testimony in the enemy’s mouth; he does not break promises. One hiding under the camel’s belly beneath the tree, and the Prophet’s {{1}} hand stretched out on behalf of the absent ‘Uthman. The surah that descended on the way back, whose name is ‘Victory’, for the journey many thought a defeat. The signet ring for Rome. The three commanders who came out of Quraysh’s house, one of whom had said, how much longer? The letter kept in al-Muqawqis’s ivory box and the consent withheld. Hawdhah’s bargaining and al-Harith’s thrown-away letter. An Ansari who waited on a broken leg for the rooster to crow. The word which, if kept, brings loss, if broken no one will ever know; the test is exactly there. So take one deed home from today’s dars.
blocks.44: Abu Jandal in chains had to be returned, yet the Prophet {{1}} did not break the word given. Today I will ask myself a question: in the matter where keeping my word would cost me and breaking it no one would ever know, what do I do? Today I will keep one promise which, if broken, no one would have said anything; I will not give up this habit of keeping a word given from today.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 2092 (from Anas (RA): ‘when the Prophet {{1}} wished to write to Rome, the Companions said, they do not read any letter without a seal; so he had a silver ring made… its design was “Muhammad Rasul Allah”’). Sahih al-Bukhari 3106, 5878 (Anas: the design was in three lines, ‘Muhammad’ one line, ‘Rasul’ one line, ‘Allah’ one line). Sahih al-Bukhari 5877 (the Prophet {{2}} said, I have had a ring made, had it engraved ‘Muhammad Rasul Allah’; let no one make this design). The making of the seal was in the period after the treaty; the sahih hadith gives no definite mention of the time; the beginning of sending letters is in this period, Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 571–572 and Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma‘ad 3/60.
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 1774 (from Anas (RA): ‘the Prophet {{1}} wrote letters to Kisra, Qaysar, the Najashi and every powerful ruler, calling them to Allah’). In one narration there is an extra sentence, ‘this Najashi is not that Najashi whose funeral prayer the Prophet {{2}} prayed’; in another narration the sentence is absent. Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 574–578: there is disagreement about the letter to the Najashi; some think it was the letter of the time of the first hijrah to Habashah (in the hand of Ja‘far (RA)), some that it was written to Ashamah, some to his successor. In this dars the Najashi’s reaction is not told.
footnotes.2: Sirah-based: Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 578–580 (Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma‘ad 3/61 also mentions this letter). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. Muqawqis is a title; the name is disputed among the Sirah scholars (Juraij ibn Matta, according to others Binyamin; al-Rahiq, p. 578, note 568). Hatib ibn Abi Balta‘ah (RA) was the envoy. The two maidservants of the gift were named Mariyah and Sirin; in Mariyah’s house Ibrahim was later born, Sirin the Prophet {{1}} gave to Hassan ibn Thabit (RA) (al-Rahiq, p. 580). That Muqawqis did not accept Islam is also in al-Rahiq.
footnotes.3: Sahih al-Bukhari 7 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA), Abu Sufyan’s own narration). The event was during the term of the Treaty of Hudaybiyah, Abu Sufyan himself told it.
footnotes.4: Part of the same Sahih al-Bukhari 7 (question and answer).
footnotes.5: Part of the same Sahih al-Bukhari 7 (Heraclius’s analysis and remarks).
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari 7 (the text of the Prophet’s {{1}} letter). At the end of the letter Surah Al ‘Imran 3:64 is quoted.
footnotes.7: The end part of the same Sahih al-Bukhari 7. ‘Ibn Abi Kabshah’ is a contemptuous nickname the polytheists used for the Prophet {{1}}; ‘Banu al-Asfar’ is a name for the Romans.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4424, 64, 7264 (from ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Abbas (RA)): the Prophet {{1}} sent his letter to Kisra with ‘Abdullah ibn Hudhafah al-Sahmi (RA); he instructed him to give it into the hand of the ruler of Bahrain; he delivered it to Kisra; Kisra read it and tore it. Ibn al-Musayyib says, the Prophet {{2}} then made du‘a against them that they be torn completely to shreds (there is a word of doubt of the kind ‘I think Ibn al-Musayyib said’ on the narrator’s part, so the du‘a part rests on the narrator’s impression).
footnotes.9: Musnad Ahmad 20438 (from Abu Bakrah (RA); Shu‘ayb al-Arna’ut: sahih): ‘a Persian man came to the Prophet {{1}}; he said: inna rabbi qad qatala rabbaka, ya‘ni Kisra (my Lord has killed your lord, that is, Kisra). And he was informed that Kisra had made his daughter successor; then he said, a people that makes a woman ruler never succeeds.’ That the speaker is the Prophet {{2}} is clear in another sahih narration: from Dihyah al-Kalbi (RA) ‘go to your companion, tell him, my Lord has killed his lord, Kisra, tonight’ (Sahih al-Jami‘ 862, al-Albani: sahih), also ‘you two tell your companion’ (Silsilah Sahihah 1429). In the text of Ahmad the subject of the word ‘faqala’ is not linguistically clear; in this dars, on the basis of the parallel sahih narrations, the speaker is taken to be the Prophet {{3}} (in al-Wadi‘i’s Sahih Dala’il al-Nubuwwah 177 the same statement with the words ‘rabbi tabaraka wa ta‘ala’; the commentaries have not examined this question separately). The hadith gives no date for when Kisra was killed.
footnotes.10: Sahih al-Bukhari 3121 (from Jabir ibn Samurah (RA)): ‘when Kisra is destroyed there is no Kisra after him, when Qaysar is destroyed there is no Qaysar after him; by the One in whose hand is my soul, their treasures will certainly be spent in the way of Allah.’ It is in Sahih Muslim too. The hadith gives no date for when it was said.
footnotes.11: How many days it took for Kisra’s empire to break is not numbered in the hadith; ‘before two decades had passed’ is a calculation: Hudaybiyah was 6 AH, and the fall of the Persian empire was in ‘Umar (RA)’s time, in the early 20s of the Hijri years (Nihawand 21 AH, by the reckoning of history books), that is, in under twenty years.

Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.13: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), pp. 589–590 (al-Harith ibn Abi Shimr al-Ghassani and Shuja‘ ibn Wahb al-Asadi; Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma‘ad 3/63). Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence. The incident of ‘Amr ibn al-‘As (RA)’s embassy to Jayfar and ‘Abd ibn al-Julandi of Oman has been called by al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (pp. 590–594) an event after the conquest of Makkah, so it has been kept outside this dars’s boundary.
footnotes.14: Sahih al-Bukhari 4039 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA); ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik’s own words: ‘I reached the Prophet {{1}} and informed him, he said, stretch out your leg…’).
footnotes.15: Sahih al-Bukhari 4039, 4038 (from al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib (RA)): the Prophet {{1}} sent several of the Ansar to Abu Rafi‘ the Jew, the leader of the group ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik; Abu Rafi‘ ‘used to hurt the Prophet {{2}} and help against him’, lived in a fortress of the Hijaz. The fortress gate, the bunch of keys, the doors one after another inside, the blow recognising the voice in the dark, the leg broken while going down, bound with a turban, ‘the rooster crowed, then a herald stood on the wall and announced: I announce the death of Abu Rafi‘, the merchant of the Hijaz’, reaching his companions ‘hurry, Allah has killed Abu Rafi‘’, telling it to the Prophet {{3}}, ‘stretch out your leg’, wiping it, ‘as if he had never been ill’. The Bukhari text does not mention the year; there is disagreement among Sirah scholars about the year of the event. According to the index the event of this dars; the Abu Rafi‘ of the fortress at Khaybar (Sallam ibn Abi al-Huqayq) and the Abu Rafi‘ of dars 15 (the Prophet’s {{4}} slave) are not the same person.

quiz.q: Why was Abu Sufyan in Sham at the court of Heraclius?
o: As a prisoner of war in Roman hands
quiz.e: He was in Sham with a trade caravan of Quraysh.

quiz.q: What did Kisra do on receiving the Prophet’s ﷺ letter?
o: Wrote a reply and sent it
quiz.e: He read the letter and tore it up.

quiz.q: When wanting to write to Rome, what did the Companions say?
o: They cannot read Arabic at all
They do not read a letter without a seal
They will not accept any letter at all
They only listen to the envoy’s spoken word, not writing
quiz.e: Sahih Muslim 2092.

quiz.q: Which Companion took the letter to Kisra?
quiz.e: Sahih al-Bukhari 4424.

quiz.q: Which ruler sent honour and gifts in reply to the letter but did not accept Islam?
quiz.e: al-Muqawqis honoured the envoy Hatib, sent maidservants and gifts, did not change his religion.

quiz.q: Who demanded a share of ruling power in return for accepting Islam?
o: al-Harith ibn Abi Shimr of Ghassan
quiz.e: The Prophet ﷺ said, even if he asks for a piece of land I will not give it.

quiz.q: Why does the answer to ‘Does he break promises?’ get special importance in this dars?
o: Abu Sufyan had told an outright lie here
The answer came during the term of the Treaty of Hudaybiyah
Heraclius did not ask the question
It was part of the letter
quiz.e: This testimony in the enemy’s mouth came during that very treaty in which Abu Jandal was returned.

quiz.q: From the incident of the seal, what etiquette of da‘wah is understood?
o: Following the customs of the one being called
Sending an envoy instead of a letter
quiz.e: The rulers of Rome do not read a letter without a seal.

quiz.q: If someone insultingly throws away our letter or call, what is our responsibility, according to this dars?
o: To stop sending letters of da‘wah and withdraw
To deliver the call; the result is in Allah’s hand
quiz.e: Delivering the call is the duty; Kisra’s end was his own.

quiz.q: From which incident does the lesson of following the culture’s rules of the one being invited come?
o: Showing the sacrificial animals to the chief of Kinanah
The silver ring with a seal for Rome
quiz.e: The rulers of Rome do not read a letter without a seal (Muslim 2092).

quiz.q: The mistake of taking courteous behaviour and gifts as consent fits which incident?
quiz.e: Courtesy and decision are not the same thing.

quiz.q: ‘Let this much right be mine, then I will accept the truth’; which incident fits this bargaining?
o: Hawdhah’s asking for a share of power
quiz.e: The truth accepted only on conditions is no longer the accepting of truth.

quiz.q: Who was the leader of the Ansari group sent to Abu Rafi‘?
quiz.e: Bukhari 4038–4039.

quiz.q: Why did ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik wait near the fortress gate on a broken leg?
o: Waiting for the leg to heal
Waiting for the gatekeeper to sleep
To be sure of the death news
quiz.e: When the herald announced the death he set out.

quiz.q: Which lesson of avoiding spreading news without certainty is in this dars?
o: Waiting for news on a broken leg
quiz.e: ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Atik did not set out until the news was made firm in the herald’s mouth.
